move: nested frames wipe in with parallax settle, collapse inward
how: Four image frames are nested in the DOM, each inset within its parent. Every image pushes from scale 1.0 to 1.12 linearly across D. Each frame reveals left-to-right via clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0)→inset(0 0% 0 0) with expo.out over 0.7s while sliding from x:60+20i to 0 with expo.out, staggered 0.16s from the outermost at 0.025D, so the nest reads as layers settling with parallax. A title rises from a mask, two caption rows rise staggered 0.08, a rule draws scaleX and an issue number fades in. From 0.72D the frames wipe out to inset(0 0 0 100%) innermost first with expo.in 0.32s, 0.07s apart, and the type shoves up.
adapt: Replace the four images (and per-frame filters), the title, caption rows and issue number; the nesting depth and inset offsets are CSS so change frame count by editing the frames array and DOM. Keep the 0.16s stagger and the expo.out wipes.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the nested .frame tree from shot.images plus .num, .title, .cap and .rule; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with per-frame t = (0.05 + i*0.16)/2 * D and exit at 1.45/2 * D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: clip-path inset animated on four nested layers each with a scaling background image
very short (2s) so the type barely holds
